Q: How to get the keymap of the currently used keyboard? A:

Here is documentation for the xkbcommon-x11 API.

xkbcommon-x11

You can download it via package manager xkbcommon-x11.

It only has a few functions so it shouldn't be too hard to figure out. I believe this gets a keymap for a device.

The XKB extension supports using separate keymaps and states for different keyboard devices. The devices are identified by an integer device ID and are managed by another X11 extension, XInput. The original X11 protocol only had one keyboard device, called the core keyboard, which is still supported as a virtual device

Q: How to set journaling mode in Python 3.12 and Sqlite3 with autocommit=False A:

Based on the docs, which say that the setting is persistent, you could just write the setting in a first round, either in Python or the sqlite program https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html#:~:text=3%2E3%2E%20Persistence%20of%20WAL%20mode,-Unlike

db = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
db.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL')
db.close()

db = sqlite3.connect(db_path, autocommit=False)
db.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL')  # now succeeds as already set
...

Assuming you always want the setting, you might even make this a somewhat-ugly dance into a wrapper

Q: problem having creating a sub routine for outputing string dynamicly without using stack in x86-64 A:

but i wanted the sub routine without stack

The only thing I see that you avoid is not having push rax nor pop rsi.
For that to happen you changed the calling register from RAX to RCX, but this time you forgot that the counting loop had left RCX pointing at the terminating zero instead of at the start of the message.

The quickest solution is to replace the push rax instruction by mov rsi, rax (before the counting loop) and just remove that pop rsi.

Next is an alternative solution that additionally can deal with zero-length messages!
Tip: when you know beforehand that the syscall expects the length in the RDX register, then why not use RDX already in the counting loop?

section .data
output1 db "hello world",10,0
output2 db "hello world again",10,0

section .bss

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    mov  rax, output1
    call _output    

    mov  rax, output2
    call _output

    call _exit  

_output:
_output_setup:
    mov  rsi, rax       ; Start of the message kept in RSI
    xor  edx, edx       ; This clears RDX
    dec  rdx
_output_length_loop:
    inc  rdx
    cmp  byte [rsi+rdx], 0
    jne  _output_length_loop
_output_output:
    mov  edi, 1         ; This makes RDI=1
    mov  eax, 1         ; This makes RAX=1
    syscall
    ret

_exit:
    xor  edi, edi       ; This clears RDI
    mov  eax, 60        ; This makes RAX=60
    syscall
    ret
